timeline_events.title: Manufactured — Ovation, USA
timeline_events.description: Ovation Elite 1868, black finish, Lyrachord bowl back. Produced in the 1990s at the Ovation factory in New Hartford, Connecticut.

timeline_events.title: Same model played at KISS MTV Unplugged
timeline_events.description: Bruce Kulick used the identical model and color — Ovation Elite 1868 in black — during the KISS MTV Unplugged performance in 1995. Documented from broadcast footage.

timeline_events.title: A dream since age 14 — finally acquired
timeline_events.description: The owner had wanted this exact guitar since approximately age 14, inspired by seeing Bruce Kulick play it at KISS Unplugged. After years of dreaming, he purchased the exact model and color.

timeline_events.title: First video — 'Forever' solo by Bruce Kulick
timeline_events.description: Owner recorded and uploaded his first video with this guitar, performing the acoustic solo from the KISS song 'Forever' — the same solo Bruce Kulick played at the 1995 Unplugged.

story.context: Owner dreamed of this guitar since age 14. Recently purchased it — the exact model and color Bruce Kulick played at KISS MTV Unplugged in 1995.
story.original_text_translated: Not long ago I bought a guitar I've wanted since about age 14, an Ovation Elite from the nineties, the exact model Bruce Kulick played at KISS Unplugged. Even the same color. In my opinion, the MTV Unplugged of KISS has the best guitar sound of any Unplugged, and forgive me Clapton, Nirvana, and Alice in Chains. For the first video I'm uploading with this guitar I chose a solo that Bruce Kulick played on acoustic guitar, from the song Forever.
story.summary: A dream since age 14 fulfilled — Ovation Elite just like Bruce Kulick's at KISS Unplugged
story.narrative: A lifelong dream since age 14 — this black Ovation Elite 1868 is the exact model and color Bruce Kulick played at KISS MTV Unplugged in 1995. The owner believes that KISS Unplugged has the best guitar sound of any Unplugged performance ever, above Clapton, Nirvana, and Alice in Chains.
notable_events: KISS MTV Unplugged 1995 — same model and color used by Kulick

images.caption: 1954 Gibson Les Paul Goldtop — front, in original Lifton case

timeline_events.title: Manufactured — Gibson, Kalamazoo, 1954
timeline_events.description: First full production year with the wraparound stud bridge/tailpiece. Brazilian rosewood fingerboard, P-90 soapbar pickups, nitrocellulose lacquer gold finish.
timeline_events.source: Model specifications and Gibson production records

timeline_events.title: Acquired in original Lifton case
timeline_events.description: Guitar found with its original brown Lifton case with purple lining — a strong provenance indicator for 1954 Les Pauls.

timeline_events.title: One year of searching — 25 guitars examined
timeline_events.description: The owner spent a full year searching before acquiring this guitar, personally examining approximately 25 examples. At 70+ years old, every instrument differs in condition, sound, neck feel, pickup originality, and repair history.

story.context: Owner searched for a full year, examining approximately 25 examples before finding the right one.
story.original_text_translated: It took a year to find it, I tried about 25. 1954 LP.
story.summary: A year of searching, 25 examples examined — until the perfect 1954 Goldtop was found
story.narrative: One year of searching. Approximately 25 guitars examined. When it comes to a 70-year-old instrument, every one is different — the condition, the sound, the feel of the neck, whether the pickups are original, whether there were repairs. The owner kept looking until finding The One. A 1954 Gibson Les Paul Goldtop in its original brown Lifton case with purple lining.

images.caption: 1970 Fender Stratocaster — heavily worn sunburst, with Gibson Les Paul and SG in background

timeline_events.title: Manufactured — Fender, Fullerton, 1970
timeline_events.description: Last year of the 4-bolt neck plate, original synchronized tremolo with steel saddles, and heel-adjust truss rod. The last Stratocaster fully aligned with Leo Fender's original design.
timeline_events.source: Model specifications and Fender production records

timeline_events.title: Father buys Strat for his 8-year-old son — France
timeline_events.description: While on a posting in France, the owner's father went searching with his son's first guitar teacher. At a second-hand shop, the teacher spotted this 1970 Stratocaster. The father pulled out cash on the spot, fulfilling his own lifelong dream of owning a Fender through his son.

timeline_events.title: 29 years of continuous ownership — primary guitar
timeline_events.description: The guitar has been with the owner since age 8 and remains his number one instrument. Every scratch and ding is genuine — not relic. 'My hand has taken the shape of its neck.'

story.context: Owner received the guitar from his father at age 8 while living in France. The father was a former guitarist who never owned a Fender — those were only for the rich.
story.original_text_translated: My Strat... This is a '70 Strat that my father bought me in France when I was 8. My father is also a former guitarist... in the past he had lots of European guitars like Hofner and Eko, but never a Fender. Fenders were only for the rich... After a few second-hand shops, the teacher saw this Strat and was captivated... My father immediately pulled out cash and bought it on the spot. This is my first guitar since I started learning to play, and it's been with me for 29 years now, and absolutely my number one guitar. You could say my hand took the shape of its neck.... All the dings are of course not relic... haha
story.summary: First guitar — father bought for his 8-year-old son in France, 29 years together, all wear genuine not relic
story.narrative: A father who grew up playing Hofner and Eko guitars — European brands that were within reach — but never a Fender. Fender was only for the rich. During a posting in France, he decided his 8-year-old son should learn guitar. The teacher spotted this 1970 Stratocaster and was mesmerized. The father immediately pulled out cash — fulfilling his own dream through his son. 29 years later, every scratch, every ding is real.
notable_events: Father's first Fender — fulfilled a lifelong dream

images.caption: Owner with his 1973-74 Natural Stratocaster — Nazareth Illit, late 1980s / early 1990s

timeline_events.title: Manufactured — Fender, Fullerton, 1973-74
timeline_events.description: CBS-era Stratocaster with 3-bolt neck plate and Micro-Tilt adjustment, bullet truss rod, large headstock. Natural/Blonde finish typically paired with Ash body.
timeline_events.source: Model specifications and Fender production records

timeline_events.title: Midnight purchase in Rishon LeZion with friend Igor
timeline_events.description: Recently discharged soldier, age 20-21, drove from Nazareth Illit to Rishon LeZion with his friend Igor. Arrived at midnight, short on cash. The seller: 'You show up at midnight AND you're short on money?' The deal worked out. Paid $600-700.

timeline_events.title: Sold — owner does not remember to whom or why
timeline_events.description: The guitar was sold at a young age. The owner regrets the decision and does not recall the buyer or the reason.

timeline_events.title: Owner searching — TWNG community alert
timeline_events.description: Original owner posted publicly seeking information about the current whereabouts of this guitar. Natural/Blonde finish, maple neck, purchased in Rishon LeZion. Last known location: Israel.

searching.reason_sold: Unknown — owner regrets selling at a young age
searching.distinguishing_features: Natural/Blonde finish, maple neck, purchased in Rishon LeZion late at night

story.context: Recently discharged soldier, age 20-21, living in Nazareth Illit. Drove with friend Igor to Rishon LeZion at midnight. Short on cash. The seller was shocked but relented.
story.original_text_translated: Hello friends, that's me in the photo, a recently discharged soldier age 20-21 with my first Fender in Nazareth Illit (Nof HaGalil today). Looking for the guitar I sold — don't remember to whom or why... I drove with my friend Igor to Rishon LeZion, by the time we found the address we arrived at midnight, I was also short a few shekels, the seller said: 'You show up at midnight AND you're short on money' haha. In the end it worked out nicely and he let it go. Yes, I made a mistake selling it at a young age, I made a few mistakes... Fender year '73 or '74.
story.summary: First Strat, bought on a midnight adventure in Rishon LeZion — sold regretfully, owner searching
story.narrative: Midnight. Rishon LeZion, Israel. A recently discharged soldier arrives with his friend Igor. They're short on cash. The seller: 'You show up at midnight AND you're short on money?' But the deal gets done. $600, maybe $700. They drive back with a 1973-74 Fender Stratocaster, natural finish, maple neck. Years later, he sold it. Doesn't remember to whom. Now he's searching.
notable_events: Midnight purchase in Rishon LeZion with friend Igor
Sold — owner searching for this guitar
